subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ACME follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>, Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ACME follow-up

Hi Alice / Bob -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment for the Private/VPC performance qualification: 

1) SLO targets you shared
   - P50 latency target: ~40ms
   - P95 latency target: 200ms (for single-token responses) - you noted some flows need stricter p95s (we captured a few below)
   - Throughput: ~1,200 requests/min sustained, spiking to ~3,500/min during peak campaigns
   - Concurrent streams: up to 200 concurrent streaming sessions

2) Streaming requirements
   - Partial token streaming is required for real-time UI responsiveness (low-latency first-byte)

3) Private/VPC details we need to qualify performance and network path
   - Confirmation of peering method (AWS VPC peering, Direct Connect, or site-to-site VPN)
   - Expected egress destinations (Redwood endpoint IP ranges / regions) and whether traffic will traverse public internet
   - Internal latency budgets (app -> inference stack) and whether you have a preferred cross-AZ or single-AZ setup

4) Next steps / asks (action owners & timelines)
   - ACME: Share network diagram and routing details (VPC/subnet/peering) - Alice/Bob by EOD Tue 8/25
   - Redwood (Dev): Provide VPC checklist & recommended TCP/TLS settings and perform a quick network test once diagram is shared - by Fri 8/28
   - Redwood (Marissa): Draft mutual action plan & estimated cost delta for Dedicated/Private modes - Tue 8/25

Attachments: network-requirements-matrix.xlsx (high-level matrix we use to map SLOs -> config)

If anything above is off, flag and I'll update. Otherwise we'll wait for your topology and Dev will pick this up.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Note: For performance testing we typically recommend keeping app-to-inference RTT below ~60ms to give headroom for tokenization and downstream processing. We'll call this out in the VPC checklist.

From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ACME follow-up

Thanks Marissa - very helpful recap. Answers inline: 

- Peering: We plan to use AWS Direct Connect to a Transit Gateway; we currently peer several vendors over Direct Connect (not VPN) but can fall back to site-to-site VPN for initial tests.
- Egress: Traffic will originate from our app VPC in us-west-2 and should prefer private peering to Redwood's us-west endpoint. If Direct Connect isn't available during test windows, traffic will go over internet egress through our NAT Gateway (we'll note that).
- Internal latency budget: We aim for app -> inference <= 80ms on average; critical interactive flows want <= 50ms avg and p95 <= 150ms.
- Concurrency / throughput: Confirming the numbers Marissa wrote - sustained 1.2k/min, burst to 3.5k/min, ~200 concurrent streaming connections.
- TLS/profile: Can you share supported cipher suites and whether mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported for Private deployments?

Attached our current topology export (acme-network-topology.pdf) - it's high-level but shows Direct Connect -> TGW -> app VPC. We'll follow up with subnet-level routing and egress ACLs.

We'll aim to have the detailed diagram and peering contacts by Tuesday (8/25).

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
alice@acme.com

[attachment: acme-network-topology.pdf]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification - ACME follow-up

Hi Alice/Marissa -

Thanks for the topology file, Alice - that helps. A few technical clarifications and recommendations from the Redwood infra/SE side: 

- mTLS: Supported for Private deployments. We can provision certs via your PKI or use our managed cert rotation; recommend mTLS for Direct Connect peering.
- TLS/ciphers: We support modern TLS 1.2+ profiles (AES-GCM suites, ECDHE key exchange). If you have a specific corporate policy we'll validate compatibility - please share the cipher list.
- Latency budgeting: Marissa's note on keeping app->inference RTT <60ms is a good target. Given your target of 50ms for critical flows, we recommend:
   * App -> edge (Redwood ingress in same AZ): <= 30ms
   * Edge -> inference runtime (GPU pool): <= 20ms
   * Kernel/queue overhead: <10ms (this is variable by model/sequence length)

- Network tests we typically run:
   1) TCP handshake + TLS handshake time to the target IPs
   2) ICMP + UDP path for jitter measurements (if allowed)
   3) Small HTTP/1.1 POSTs exercising streaming responses to validate first-byte latency

- Peering: Direct Connect to our Transit (preferred). If you initially route over NAT for the test, please mark that and we'll account for additional NAT latency in our analysis.

Attached the Redwood VPC checklist and a one-page recommended config for streaming workloads (redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf). Once you share subnet-level routing and a traceroute to the proposed endpoint IPs, we can schedule a short network validation (30-60 minutes) and an initial qps/load test to measure p95 under real conditions.

Thanks - copying Jordan to coordinate scheduling.

-Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
[attachment: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf]
